name: Durgakant Pushp
intro: I study adaptive robotic intelligence under limits on information, computation, time, and energy. My research connects what a robot can physically do, how it represents the world, and how it chooses its actions.
bio: I am a postdoctoral researcher in the School of Mechanical Engineering at Purdue University, working with Purdue AI Racing. I earned my Ph.D. in Intelligent Systems Engineering at Indiana University Bloomington, advised by Prof. Lantao Liu. Previously, I led the IU–Luddy Autonomous Racing Team and worked on visual navigation, heterogeneous robotic systems, and bounded-rational decision-making.
vision: When a robot cannot accomplish a task, what should it change? My research studies intelligence as a coupled search over embodiment, representation, and policy. The goal is to distinguish physical limitations from limitations of information or strategy, and to adapt economically within the resources available.
teaching_statement: My teaching and mentoring connect foundational ideas with the practical demands of building autonomous systems. I help students move between mathematical models, software implementation, and physical experiments, with attention to clear reasoning, independent problem solving, and careful evaluation.
mentoring_statement: I mentor researchers through problem formulation, implementation, experimentation, and manuscript development. My experience includes graduate, undergraduate, and high-school students working on perception, navigation, localization, and complete robotic systems.
